_comment: Exceptions to the idempotency rules enforced by scripts/check-migration-idempotency.cjs.
This is the ONLY way to suppress a rule. A "-- idempotent: …" comment in the SQL
suppresses nothing — comments are masked out before any rule runs, precisely so a claim
about a statement can never be mistaken for a guard on it.
Entry shape: { file, line, rule, reason, added_by, baseline? }
file      repo-relative path, e.g. "Backend/src/schema/migrations/013_....sql"
line      1-indexed line the violation is reported on
rule      "R1" … "R13"
reason    why this statement genuinely cannot be guarded
added_by  who accepted the risk
baseline  optional. true = pre-existing debt recorded when a rule was introduced,
NOT a clearance. Every entry, baseline or not, is PRINTED on every run.
The guard FAILS if a hand-written entry no longer matches a real violation (stale-
suppression rot), so entries cannot quietly outlive the code they excuse. A BASELINE
entry that stops matching means somebody actually guarded the statement — the outcome the
rule exists to produce — so that is reported as "BASELINE RESOLVED" and does NOT fail the
build; delete the entry (or re-run --write-baseline) in that change or the next one.
The R13 entries below are the unguarded UPDATE/DELETE statements that already existed
across the 85 released migrations when R13 was written. They are DEBT, not approval —
read each reason; they are not interchangeable. The three 074 entries are the one
exception: that file's de-dup was fixed (verification finding #6) and its DELETEs are
convergent, just not in a shape a static checker can prove. 059 (finding #5) needed no
entry at all — it now carries a real NOT EXISTS guard.
extraction_mode carries ZERO R13 debt as of this change, and that is the point of
verification finding #12. master_options.extraction_mode is a live COST dial — it decides
whether a document category goes to Tesseract or to a per-page Claude Vision call — so an
unguarded re-assertion of it is a migration that silently reverts an operator's spend
decision. Every statement that writes the column is now guarded `AND extraction_mode IS
NULL`: migration 052 (eleven statements, guarded earlier — those eleven baseline entries
have been deleted here), migration 050 (two statements) and migration 051 (one, which was
split out of a combined extraction_mode + description UPDATE so that guarding the dial
would not also freeze the prompt hint). Their four baseline entries are gone from this
file because the debt is gone, not because it was excused.
What remains for 051 is three description-only UPDATEs. `description` keeps the OPPOSITE
precedence on purpose (seed 010 resolves it as COALESCE(EXCLUDED, existing) — the catalog
wins), so those statements stay unguarded and stay recorded here, same class as 049.
Re-anchor line numbers after a migration edit with:
node scripts/check-migration-idempotency.cjs --write-baseline R13 --added-by "<who>"
(reasons already recorded for a file are preserved).

re-asserts a committed master_options.description prompt hint over whatever the table holds, so a replay overwrites a hand-tuned hint (same class as 049). This is DELIBERATE and is the documented precedence for this column: seeds/010_master_options_doc_category.sql resolves description as COALESCE(EXCLUDED, existing) — the catalog wins — because retuning a hint is the routine, reviewed way extraction quality improves and re-asserting one costs nothing. NOT the same as extraction_mode, which is operator-owned and is now guarded `AND extraction_mode IS NULL` in every statement of 050, 051 and 052. Recorded as accepted debt, not cleared: an operator who hand-edits a description still loses it on a replay.

entries.reason: REVIEWED, not debt: verification finding #6 has been fixed in this file — the de-dup now keeps the EARLIEST ctid and matches on ALL non-key columns (IS NOT DISTINCT FROM), so it removes only byte-identical re-seeded rows and a replay finds none left to remove. It is convergent, but the convergence lives in the join predicate rather than in an IF wrapper or a NOT EXISTS clause, which is the only shape R13 can verify statically. Re-check this entry if the DELETE predicate changes.
